# Lab 18.11: Find PII with Sensitive Data Protection

## What We Are Going to Do
Run a Sensitive Data Protection discovery scan on BigQuery, read the data profiles, and use the findings to decide which columns need policy tags.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Enable the API.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud services enable dlp.googleapis.com</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[Console] Create a discovery scan.** **Security → Sensitive Data Protection → Discovery → Enable / Create scan configuration**:
   - **Type**: BigQuery
   - **Scope**: project `bq-course-lab`
   - **Schedule**: profile new tables, re-profile on schema change
   - **Actions**: save profiles to BigQuery dataset `lab18_dlp`

3. **[Console] Read the profiles.** After the scan, open **Data profiles**. `lab18_private.users` shows **High** sensitivity with **EMAIL_ADDRESS** in the `email` column.

4. **[SQL] Query the saved profiles.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT table_data_profile.full_resource AS table_name, column_profile.column, column_profile.info_type.name AS info_type, column_profile.sensitivity_score.score AS sensitivity
FROM lab18_dlp.`*`
WHERE column_profile.info_type.name IS NOT NULL
LIMIT 20;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The exact table name and columns are shown in the dataset after the first scan; adjust the query to match.

5. **Act on the findings.** For each high-sensitivity column, add the **PII** policy tag (Lab 18.5) and a masking rule (Lab 18.6).

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Discovery | Automatic profiling of BigQuery tables |
| Finding | `email` → EMAIL_ADDRESS, high sensitivity |
| Output | Profiles saved to BigQuery |
| Next step | Policy tags and masking |
